newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says Iraq-based rebels send "sabotage" teams.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Iraq-based rebels send "sabotage" teams.

text.p: Iran accused on Wednesday an Iraq-based armed opposition group of training dozens of squads to carry out sabotage in Iranian cities.
An unnamed security official told the Iranian news agency IRNA that the Mujahideen Khalq group had set up some 45 teams of two to four members each for the attacks.

Iraqi officials had helped the team members, who had arms and explosives and carried forged identity cards, to cross the border into Iran, the Iranian official said. The report did not say how many of the alleged squads were already in Iran.

Iran said on Monday its forces had killed four Mujahideen members outside the border town of Mehran and three others, a woman and two men, in a shootout in Sari, 110 km (70 miles) northeast of Tehran.
The Mujahideen said their forces based inside Iran had killed or wounded "a large number" of troops in clashes in Sari and in Ilam province, where Mehran is located.
The group denied four of its members were killed in Mehran and did not report any casualties in its ranks in Sari.

Tehran has said its troops killed several Mujahideen members in clashes in western Iran in the past few weeks. The Mujahideen have admitted that some of their forces were killed but said they had slain or wounded "hundreds" of government troops.
Iran has not reported any casualties among its forces.

Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years. The Mujahideen have denied attacking civilians, but have taken responsibility for hitting military, government and economic targets.

Iraqi newspapers said on Wednesday Iraq had asked the United Nations to put pressure on Iran to either put on trial or hand over the attackers who tried to kill President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday. Iran has denied Iraqi allegations that it was involved in the attack.
Iran and Iraq, which fought a war from 1980 to 1988, often accuse each other of backing rebel groups from the other country.
